source_evidence.observation: The paper defines F = {m·β^e : m,e ∈ ℤ, −β^p < m < β^p, e_min ≤ e ≤ e_max}. Unless stated otherwise, operations use rounding to nearest. FastTwoSum computes s ← x ⊕ y, t ← s ⊖ x, and e ← y ⊖ t.

An exponent e(f) belongs to a representation f = m_f·β^{e(f)} satisfying equation (1), and representations need not be unique. The FastTwoSum exact-decomposition conclusion is s + e = x + y with s = x ⊕ y.

For r ∈ (−β^{e_max+p}, β^{e_max+p}), ulp(r) is min{g−f : f,g ∈ F ∪ {β^{e_max+p}}, f ≤ |r| < g}. Thus the inequalities in equations (17) and the Lemma 4 proof use spacing measured at the exact real product.

For FastTwoSum inputs x,y ∈ F, nearest addition and faithful subtraction suffice if some representation of x satisfies |y| ≤ ⌈β^p − β/2⌉ β^{e(x)}. The ceiling encloses the entire expression β^p − β/2, and the inequality is non-strict.

Throughout Section 4, p is the mantissa length, β is the base, and e_min,e_max give the feasible exponent range. Operations are rounded to nearest unless otherwise specified, overflow is generally assumed absent, and any base restriction or underflow exception is stated separately.

FourSumThreeProduct performs (t_h,t_l) ← TwoProduct(x_2,x_3), (s_1,s'_2) ← TwoProduct(x_1,t_h), and (s'_3,s'_4) ← TwoProduct(x_1,t_l). TwoProduct is used as an error-free two-term product transformation when neither underflow nor overflow occurs.

Equation (17) states t_h+t_l=x_2·x_3, t_h=x_2⊙x_3, and |t_l|≤(1/2)ulp(x_2·x_3). The analogous contracts for the other two TwoProduct calls imply s_1+Σ_{i=2}^4 s'_i=Π_{i=1}^3 x_i. ThreeProduct then calls FourSumThreeProduct, calls FastTwoSum on (s'_2,s'_3) to obtain (s_2,s''_3), and computes s_3←s''_3⊕s'_4. Lemma 4 assumes absence of underflow errors within FourSumThreeProduct and concludes Σ_{i=1}^3 s_i=Π_{i=1}^3 x_i.

source_evidence.anchor: condition (7), FastTwoSum merge, and exact final addition
source_evidence.observation: The proof obtains a representation of s'_2 with β^{e(s'_2)}≥ulp(t_h) and proves |s'_3|≤β^p|t_l|≤(1/2)β^p ulp(t_h)≤(1/2)β^pβ^{e(s'_2)}≤⌈β^p−β/2⌉β^{e(s'_2)}. Hence condition (7) gives s_2+s''_3=s'_2+s'_3. It then proves |s''_3|≤(1/2)β^p and |s''_3+s'_4|≤β^p; the integer s''_3+s'_4 lies in F, so s_3=s''_3+s'_4 is evaluated without error.

contract_plain_english: For three floating-point inputs, run three TwoProduct transformations to obtain an exact four-term expansion of x_1x_2x_3. Merge the middle terms s'_2 and s'_3 with FastTwoSum. The proof establishes the exact condition |s'_3|≤⌈β^p−β/2⌉β^{e(s'_2)} for a feasible representation of s'_2, so this merge is error-free for arbitrary base β. The remaining residual s''_3 and s'_4 have an exact sum lying in F, making the final rounded addition exact. Consequently, under Section 4's no-overflow convention and Lemma 4's absence-of-underflow-errors assumption for FourSumThreeProduct, the three returned values satisfy s_1+s_2+s_3=x_1x_2x_3 exactly. [PDF pp. 9 and 13-15, printed pp. 391 and 395-397, anchors: Section 4 conventions, equations (17)-(18), condition (7) proof, and final exact addition]
